top.title: ILT20 Season 5 introduces new batter zone Wide rule and two-way 60-second stop clock
top.description: The upcoming fifth season of the International League T20 will feature significant changes to its playing conditions, with a new "batter zone" to determine Wide deliveries and the extension of the 60-second stop clock to the batting side. The revised regulations, which come into effect from the opening match on November 21, aim to ensure greater consistency in umpiring decisions and maintain a faster pace of play. The introduction of the batter zone marks one of the biggest changes. Under the new rule, a delivery will be called Wide if the entire ball passes outside the designated zone between the off-side and leg-side wide lines at the popping crease. A delivery passing above the standing batter’s head height will also be deemed a Wide. The rule will apply even if a batter moves across the crease to reach the delivery, provided no part of the ball passes within the designated zone and the batter makes no contact. An exception will apply to reverse sweeps and switch hits, for which the existing off-side Wide lines will be used. Another notable change concerns the 60-second stop clock, which will now apply to both batting and fielding teams. Previously enforced only on the fielding side, the regulation requires both batters to be ready for the next over within 60 seconds of the previous over ending. Teams will receive two warnings per innings. From the third offence onwards, the fielding side will be awarded five penalty runs. Certain situations, including injury treatment, strategic time-outs, weather interruptions and third-umpire reviews, will be exempt. The playing conditions also strengthen opportunities for regional cricketers. Each Playing XI must include at least two UAE players, two Afghanistan players and one player from an ICC Associate Member nation. This minimum combination must be maintained during substitutions and Super Sub changes, with specific provisions for concussion replacements. The fifth edition of the tournament will run from November 21 to December 20, 2026, featuring six franchises and several prominent international players.

top.description: Mandatory Credit: Brad Mills-Imagn Images Washington Wizards star Anthony Davis spent five and a half seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers , and it appears he might want a reunion. Brian Windhorst recently appeared on ESPN LA’s The Sedano & Kap Morning Show , where co-host Scott Kaplan told him he’d overheard reporters in the media room at a Lakers game talking about Davis wanting to come back to Los Angeles. “They don’t realize I’m listening and I’m hearing what they’re saying,” Kaplan said. “[One of them said], ‘I hear that Anthony Davis wants to return to the Lakers.’… I think they’re credentialized. I think they know what they’re talking about. They assume I have no idea. But Windy, could Anthony Davis… We always talk about another big man for the Lakers. “A, have you heard it?” Kaplan continued. “And B, is there a world where that could happen?” Windhorst rightly pointed out that Kaplan was talking about gossip in the press room. As for whether Davis and the Lakers could reunite, the 48-year-old doesn’t see it happening. “Very unlikely,” Windhorst said. “Anthony Davis is one of the bigger question marks in the league this year. There’s like three guys we’re watching, sort of star-level players about will they get traded. One is Anthony Davis, one is Kyrie Irving, Domantas Sabonis is on there. All of them are in the same boat. “All of them have options in their contract for next season,” Windhorst continued. “… The Wizards basically said, ‘We want to see Anthony Davis play 20 to 30 games, see how he fits with our group, and then we’re going to revisit about whether we want to give him a contract extension.’ Obviously, if they give him a contract extension, he agrees to it, he’s not being traded. “If he doesn’t get a contract extension, then I think you’re going to see his name out there on the trade market,” Windhorst added. “But here’s the thing. The Lakers just don’t have much high value things, forget about Anthony, just for any for any star player. They just don’t have much to trade. The Lakers would have to give up most of their quality role players to get to $58 million. top.description: The Dylan Larkin trade saga has taken another interesting turn, and the Boston Bruins remain a team worth watching. While the Detroit Red Wings continue searching for an acceptable return for their former captain, a source has floated a potential trade framework involving veteran center Pavel Zacha , defenseman Mason Lohrei , or a first-round draft pick. There is a catch, of course. Actually, there are several. According to reporting from James Murphy of The Sick Podcast , Boston has been pushing harder to enter the Larkin sweepstakes. However, the Bruins reportedly have no interest in surrendering prized young center James Hagens, a player Detroit is believed to covet. That raises an obvious question: Could Boston satisfy the Red Wings without sacrificing one of its most promising young players? The source wondered whether Zacha, accompanied by Lohrei or a first-round selection, could provide enough value to get Detroit interested. Importantly, this was a hypothetical framework raised by a source, not confirmation that Boston has submitted such an offer . Still, the names are worth examining. top.title: Maresca ‘concerned’ after Man City suffer third league loss in a row
top.description: Manchester City Coach Enzo Maresca gives an interview prior to the start of the UEFA Champions League soccer match between RB Leipzig and Manchester City at Red Bull Arena. (is associated with: «Maresca ‘concerned’ after Man City suffer third league loss in a row») Jan Woitas/dpa Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca is concerned about his side’s form after they suffered a third Premier League defeat in a row by going down 3-1 at Nottingham Forest. City won their opening seven games of the season but followed up defeats to Aston Villa and Brighton with a poor reverse at the City Ground. They were 2-0 down inside 18 minutes as Jair Cunha and Liam Delap scored before Rayan Cherki’s fine strike after the break gave them hope. But Delap’s second on the counter-attack killed the game and left Maresca’s side six points off leaders Arsenal. “I’m always concerned, even when we win games,” the Italian said. “We need to have balance. We won seven in a row. Now we have lost three in a row, so we need balance on that." “During the international break, try to understand what we can do better, and try to start again after the international break." “In the same way we have done the first one, we’re going to use this international break to try to clarify what we can do better," he addded. “We know we do some things better, and also we know we need to improve things. So we are going to use that and try to understand how we can avoid these kind of games,” he continued. Maresca revealed Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol were replaced at half-time due to injury. “Both injury, both asked for a change,” he said. “Marc Guehi an injury. Josko Gvardiol had some issue already during the week, so it was just because they had problems.” The victory could be a coming of age for Delap and Forest, who have struggled to adapt to life under new boss Oliver Glasner, with just one win from their opening nine games. Delap had scored once in eight games following his club-record move from Chelsea, but his brilliant double proved he can be the man to fire Forest to better things this season. “It’s now for Liam to keep working, getting into his best shape,” Glasner said. “Let’s say getting back to the Liam Delap he has been at Ipswich, and then even of course improving his game and he has still a lot to improve. “Definitely not his finishing with left and right, but he has to improve his heading, he has to improve his movements in the box. “He has to improve his understanding what we’re doing out of possession. But, also very honestly, he did very well.” Glasner reacted to Delap’s second goal with a touchline sprint to join in the celebrations. The Austrian said: “Of course, I can’t demand from the players they have to outrun the opposition, and I run less than the opposite manager. So I think I had to follow. “I just was told they were running six or seven kilometres more than City today, and that means I had to run more than Enzo Maresca as well, and I did my job. It was funny for me.”

top.title: Indiana Pacers Can Now Afford To Sign A Free Agent. Should They?
top.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 02: Quenton Jackson #29 of the Indiana Pacers makes a move on Corey Kispert #24 of the Atlanta Hawks at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on November 02, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty Images INDIANAPOLIS – The Indiana Pacers can now afford to sign a veteran 15th player to their roster. But do they need to do it right now? That’s the question the team’s front office is considering. Entering the season, the Pacers team spending level was over the luxury tax line and, of all importance for their roster size, near the first apron. That first apron acts as a hard cap for Indiana because they used a specific salary cap exception to sign wing Kelly Oubre in the offseason. When the season began, the Pacers had $206.8 million committed in terms of guaranteed contracts and possible salary bonuses. The first apron is just over $209 million. That left the team with a bit over $2.2 million in space between their roster spending and their hard cap. The veteran’s minimum for the entire 2026-27 NBA season is just shy of $2.45 million. That meant the Pacers couldn’t even afford to sign a player to a minimum-salary agreement when the season began – only a player with zero (and drafted in the second round) or one year of service could have been added to their team at the time. As a result, the Pacers carried 14 players on their roster to begin the season. But once the regular season starts, every passing day makes minimum contracts cheaper. They pro-rate based on how much of the season remains. And so earlier this week, a veteran’s minimum contract became small enough in remaining value that the Pacers could afford to sign any available free agent to a one-year contract. But the question remains: Should they? Entering the season, the answer to an early-as-possible addition seemed like it should be no. Just because the Pacers could sign someone doesn’t mean they should. Because minimum contracts pro-rate, as noted above, every passing day gives the Pacers more flexibility. For example, if the team opted to sign a player on the first possible day they could have, and that player stayed with the team for the rest of the season, the Pacers (essentially) couldn’t take back more salary than they sent out in trades or signed a player to a 10-day contract if they opened a roster spot – among many other transactions that would have become harder or impossible by using (basically) all of their remaining apron space at the first possible instant. The Pacers can – if they’re able to keep avoiding a signing – keep more team-building avenues open by waiting. Between slightly imbalanced trades, short-term signings, and other considerations related to their Mid-Level Exception, there are plenty of reasons to wait. top.title: Chiefs Get Triple Injury Blow on Defense Before Week 9 Clash With Jets
top.description: Cornerback Mansoor Delane logged 27 tackles and an interception across five starts, while rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods added 13 tackles and a half-sack in seven games to anchor Kansas City’s defense. Behind their contributions, the Chiefs built a top-tier run defense, allowing just 96.3 rushing yards per game this season. However, following a frustrating loss to the Denver Broncos, Kansas City now faces a sudden depth crisis. The latest defensive injuries force Kansas City to shuffle its personnel ahead of the matchup against the New York Jets. Mansoor Delane and two others miss Jets clash due to injuries Heading into Week 9, the Kansas City defense faces a sudden roster crunch as official injury reports confirm three key starters will sit out the upcoming matchup against New York. Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Mansoor Delane (5) celebrates with defensive end George Karlaftis (56) after a play against the Seattle Seahawks during the first half of the game at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Chiefs confirmed the status in their Week 9 update: “Nikko Remigio is questionable to play Sunday against the New York Jets. Peter Woods, Mansoor Delane, and Omarr Norman-Lott are out,” the team announced . Woods is dealing with a neck injury, Delane has a shoulder issue and Norman-Lott is listed with a knee injury. Andy Reid said Woods and Delane are progressing, but neither will play Sunday. “Both those two… are making progress, and that’s a positive thing, but they’re going to be out this game. It’s just a matter of getting back and making sure they’re strong; both of them, it’s a strength thing right now,” Reid said. Delane’s absence removes a first-round corner from the secondary. Kansas City selected the LSU product sixth overall in 2026. He has one interception and five pass breakups. Woods was also a first-round pick. His 13 tackles, half-sack, and pass breakup have supported the interior rotation. Norman-Lott’s absence further reduces the rotation and places more work on Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga. Remigio has 274 yards on 10 kick returns and 70 yards on 12 punt returns, giving Kansas City field-position value. The Chiefs enter after a 28-24 loss in Denver, their second defeat of the season after a 5-0 start. They allowed 11 penalties for 105 yards, and personal fouls helped Denver score 18 points. Sunday’s game at Arrowhead will test Steve Spagnuolo’s rotation. The Chiefs need replacements to protect the run defense, limit big plays, and avoid short fields. Their communication will matter against a Jets offense that has scored 58 points since Week 7. top.title: 'A shared vision': LASA boys pace each other to Class 5A UIL state cross-country title
top.description: The LASA boys team, flanked by Stacia Crescenzi, LASA's principal and assistant coach Sarah Davis on the left and head cross country coach Mary Beth Metcalf and assistant coach Kitty Kistler on the right, stand on the podium after winning the Class 5A state championship at the UIL state cross-country championships at Old Settler's Park in Round Rock, Texas. (Brom Hoban/Special to American-Statesman) ROUND ROCK - Over two cool, breezy days at Old Settler's Park, more than 1,500 of the state's best high school distance runners competed in the UIL state cross-country championships. And while there were a number of standout performances from Central Texas runners, it was Austin's LASA Raptors who rose to the pinnacle, capturing first place in Saturday's Class 5A race. The Raptors were led by senior Liam Brandyberry, who finished seventh overall in 15 minutes, 28 seconds on the rolling 5K course. "It took preparation, drive, commitment, character and courage to do what they had to do today, which is not easy," LASA head cross-country coach Mary Beth Metcalf said of the boys team, which also consisted of seniors Joaquin Gonzalez, John Wilson, Cruz Alcorta and Hugo Radjef, and juniors Ben Vazquez and Sam Smith. "Not so much a tactical approach, it was more about being committed to one another," Metcalf added. "During the race, when it feels overwhelming, when they feel like maybe they can't hang on any longer, when their brains are telling them to let up, I ask them to think about one another and the love that they have for their teammates, and to let that teammate commitment be what drives them forward. Our team has a shared commitment and obligation to will it into reality. It's a shared vision." Only the top five runners from each team have their finishing places added together to calculate the team score; the team with the lowest total score wins. LASA scored 94 points, ahead of runner-up Weslaco East's 98 and third-place Dallas Wilson's 113. Weslaco East's Alexander Nava won the overall race in 15 minutes, 13 seconds, while Georgetown's Matthew Morales averaged 4:56 per mile to grab second in 15:18. Liberty Hill's Zander Radziwon was 11th (15:40) and Lockhart's Ethan Herrera (15:52) was 19th. "These boys, since they've been freshmen, they've always felt like a team and worked together like a team," LASA principal Stacia Crescenzi said. "What makes this so emotional today is not that they won, but that they did it together." It kicks off at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples on Sunday at 11.30 GMT (12.30 CET). Few expected the two teams to be in their current position going into the season, as Gennaro Gattuso’s Lazio are alone three points clear at the top of the table, where Max Allegri is facing calls for his dismissal after a series of poor results, including the 4-1 Champions League defeat to FC Porto. top.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams Hit With NFL Fines
top.description: The Detroit Lions picked up a hard-fought 19-15 victory over the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8, but two of their biggest offensive stars are now paying a price for their actions during the game. On Saturday, the NFL announced that wide receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams were each fined $11,941 for taunting during Detroit’s November 1 victory at Ford Field. That’s a combined $23,882 in fines for the Lions’ dynamic receiving duo. Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams (1) reacts to a penalty after a first down celebration against Minnesota Vikings during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit Lions Receivers Fined for Taunting According to the NFL’s official accountability report , both violations occurred during the first quarter. Amon-Ra St. Brown: $11,941 for taunting with 11:25 remaining in the first quarter. Jameson Williams: $11,941 for taunting with 4:55 remaining in the first quarter. Williams’ penalty came following a 46-yard reception from Jared Goff that moved Detroit deep into Minnesota territory. However, the receiver was flagged after spinning the football near a Vikings defender, costing the Lions 15 yards. St. Brown was penalized earlier in the quarter after standing over a Minnesota defender following a running play. Both incidents resulted in unsportsmanlike conduct penalties during the game. Jameson Williams Has Been Here Before Interestingly, this isn’t the first time Williams has found himself dealing with the NFL’s disciplinary process this season. Earlier in the year, Williams was assessed fines totaling $26,867 for taunting and an illegal celebration during Detroit’s Week 2 loss to Buffalo. However, the receiver successfully appealed both fines , resulting in those penalties being rescinded. Whether Williams or St. Brown will appeal their latest fines remains to be seen. Despite the penalties, Detroit ultimately got the result it wanted against Minnesota. As we previously reported following the victory , Williams caught the go-ahead touchdown pass from Goff in the fourth quarter, helping the Lions hand the Vikings their first loss of the season. The victory also improved Detroit’s record to 5-2, with the Lions leaning heavily on a rushing attack that piled up 230 yards . The NFL has made it clear that taunting violations can carry consequences beyond the field. For St. Brown and Williams, that lesson now comes with a combined $23,882 price tag, assuming the fines are upheld.

top.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold watches from the bench as Fede Valverde scores a stunner from right-back for Real Madrid
top.description: Valencia CF v Real Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Trent Alexander-Arnold joined Real Madrid to become their first-choice right-back, but under Jose Mourinho he is now watching a midfielder do that job instead. Captain Fede Valverde started there again at Mestalla and smashed in the opener against Valencia, while Alexander-Arnold and summer signing Denzel Dumfries were left out of the starting XI once again. Valverde strikes from right-back at Mestalla Valverde lined up at right-back for Real Madrid's trip to Valencia on Saturday, with neither Alexander-Arnold nor Dumfries in Mourinho's starting XI. The Uruguayan made the call look inspired in the 28th minute, when Kylian Mbappe's free-kick was blocked by the wall and the ball rolled back to the Real Madrid captain. Valverde controlled the ball around 20 metres out and drilled a powerful low strike into the net. Arda Guler doubled the lead eight minutes later, and the visitors went in at the break 2-0 up. Captain dominates in an unfamiliar role Valverde's display was about far more than his goal. According to Sofascore, he had 32 touches in the first half, completed 26 of his 29 passes and was not dribbled past once, while Real Madrid enjoyed 75 per cent of possession. It was the latest sign that Mourinho's experiment has become a settled plan. Valverde was first moved to right-back during the 1-0 win over Villarreal last month and has since started there against Sevilla, RB Leipzig and Barcelona, as well as at Mestalla. Alexander-Arnold's minutes dry up The shift has hit Alexander-Arnold hardest. The England international has played just 435 minutes in all competitions this season, with only four starts in La Liga, and he was an unused substitute in Real Madrid's last three Champions League games. His only start since the Villarreal game came in the 3-0 win at Racing Santander , when Valverde missed out with muscular discomfort. It is a sharp fall for a player who made 30 appearances last season despite a string of injuries, while Dumfries has also lost his place only months after arriving. What next for the sidelined full-backs? Real Madrid had won seven games in a row in all competitions before kick-off, so Mourinho has little reason to change a winning side. Speaking at his press conference before the Racing game, he insisted: "In the end, everyone will play." Alexander-Arnold can count on England. Thomas Tuchel left him out of his World Cup squad but has since recalled him, and he played 90 minutes in both wins over the Czech Republic during the last international break. England face Croatia on Thursday.

nigeria.title: Olawepo-Hashim visits Sowore, condemns political violence
nigeria.description: Former presidential candidate, Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has condemned political violence in Nigeria, warning that attacks on political opponents could worsen the country’s already precarious security situation. Olawepo-Hashim also called on President Bola Tinubu to caution members of his team against actions and statements capable of provoking political conflict. He made the remarks in a statement posted on his X platform on Saturday after visiting activist and publisher, Omoyele Sowore, following the reported attack on him in Ekiti State. Olawepo-Hashim said his visit was motivated by their longstanding relationship, which dates back to their participation in the struggle against military dictatorship and the campaign for democracy. He warned that Nigeria, already grappling with terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other security challenges, could not afford another crisis arising from political violence. “Nigeria cannot afford to add political violence to the general insecurity in the land. “Nigeria is already battling terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and widespread insecurity. We cannot afford to add political violence to this burden,” he said. The former presidential candidate welcomed a statement by a United Nations representative expressing concern over the incident and urged other international partners to condemn political violence. He also urged political leaders to exercise restraint, warning that those who provoke violence might not be the ones to suffer its consequences. “President Bola Tinubu must call his team to order. Political leaders must exercise restraint and stop actions or rhetoric capable of provoking conflict. Those who recklessly provoke violence may not be the ones who bear its consequences,” he said. Recalling their history, Olawepo-Hashim said he and Sowore had been comrades since 1989/1990, when they worked together against military rule. He said he was particularly moved by Sowore’s recollection of how he introduced him to political activism at the University of Lagos. According to him, Sowore reaffirmed during the visit that he remained undeterred by the reported attack and was determined to continue campaigning for genuine democracy. nigeria.title: Trump orders Justice Department probe of Democrats seeking impeachment
nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump said Saturday he was ordering the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration. Trump faces a radically transformed and hostile political landscape after Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and the Senate in Tuesday’s midterms. Democrats have vowed investigations into Trump and senior members of his administration, including Attorney General Todd Blanche and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. “The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people,” Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform. “This is extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable,” he said, arguing that there had been “no impeachable acts committed.” Trump said he was ordering the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act” and said “imprisonment should be against these EXTORTIONISTS.” With control of committees in both chambers, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, potentially putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny. Likely subjects include the Trump family’s business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war. “Lawyer up,” wrote incoming House Oversight Committee chairman Robert Garcia on X as the results became clear on election night. Democrats have also signaled interest in the handling of files relating to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The administration could resist demands for testimony or documents, triggering court battles. Democrats could pursue Trump’s third impeachment, though party leaders have not committed to doing so. The House needs only a simple majority to impeach, but removing a president requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate — far beyond the party’s numbers. nigeria.title: Nigeria’s Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 to win first U-17 Women’s World Cup
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, have defeated Japan 2-1 to win the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The Flamingos secured the historic victory on Saturday at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 3, in Rabat, to claim their first title in the competition. Awawu Bashiru opened the scoring for Nigeria in the 39th minute with a long-range effort that slipped through the hands of the Japanese goalkeeper. Nigeria doubled their advantage shortly after the restart, with Oluebube Umejiaku finding the net in the 47th minute to put the Flamingos in control. Japan fought back and reduced the deficit through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute. The Japanese side pushed for an equaliser, but Nigeria held on to secure the 2-1 victory. The Flamingos also came close to extending their lead late in the game, striking the crossbar from a corner kick. Road to victory Flamingos’ campaign in Morocco did not begin as expected, as the Flamingos suffered a 2-1 defeat to Poland in their opening group match. They subsequently recorded a narrow victory over Puerto Rico before producing one of the tournament’s biggest upsets by defeating defending champions DPR Korea 3-1. The Nigerian side built on that result with victories over Mexico and Venezuela before overcoming Brazil in the semi-finals to secure a historic place in the final. Nigeria are the first African country to reach the final of the competition. nigeria.description: The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, has urged his supporters to accept money offered by politicians but vote according to their conscience. nigeria.title: Rivers crisis: You’ll not regret choosing peace, Tinubu assures Fubara
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde President Bola Tinubu has assured Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, that he would not regret his decision to embrace peace and respect the intervention of political elders in resolving the crisis that rocked the state. Tinubu gave the assurance on Saturday while addressing supporters at the All Progressives Congress, APC, 2027 presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt. He said, “To me, I intervened on your behalf. Similarly, to Fubara, Your Excellency, the host governor of today, I want to thank you specifically for maturity, understanding, respect for the wisdom of elders. “When we intervened, you respected our position. You maintained peace. You are a committed democrat, Fubara. You will not regret what you have done as long as all of us are alive,” Tinubu said. The political crisis, which erupted in October 2023, followed a breakdown in relations between Fubara and his predecessor, now Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, over control of the state’s political structure. The crisis escalated in March 2025 when Tinubu declared a state of emergency in the state , suspending Fubara, his deputy, Ngozi Odu, and members of the House of Assembly for six months. Fubara returned to office in September 2025 following the expiration of the emergency rule. However, political tensions resurfaced, with lawmakers initiating another impeachment process against him and his deputy in January 2026. Efforts to reconcile the feuding camps gained momentum in June 2025 when Tinubu convened a meeting involving Fubara, Wike and members of the Rivers State House of Assembly at the Presidential Villa in Abuja. More recently, in October , Fubara and Wike held another reconciliation meeting in Port Harcourt alongside their supporters, in what was seen as an effort to consolidate the rapprochement between the two political camps. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. sports.title: ILT20 Season 5 introduces new batter zone Wide rule and two-way 60-second stop clock
sports.description: The upcoming fifth season of the International League T20 will feature significant changes to its playing conditions, with a new "batter zone" to determine Wide deliveries and the extension of the 60-second stop clock to the batting side. The revised regulations, which come into effect from the opening match on November 21, aim to ensure greater consistency in umpiring decisions and maintain a faster pace of play. The introduction of the batter zone marks one of the biggest changes. Under the new rule, a delivery will be called Wide if the entire ball passes outside the designated zone between the off-side and leg-side wide lines at the popping crease. A delivery passing above the standing batter’s head height will also be deemed a Wide. The rule will apply even if a batter moves across the crease to reach the delivery, provided no part of the ball passes within the designated zone and the batter makes no contact. An exception will apply to reverse sweeps and switch hits, for which the existing off-side Wide lines will be used. Another notable change concerns the 60-second stop clock, which will now apply to both batting and fielding teams. Previously enforced only on the fielding side, the regulation requires both batters to be ready for the next over within 60 seconds of the previous over ending. Teams will receive two warnings per innings. From the third offence onwards, the fielding side will be awarded five penalty runs. Certain situations, including injury treatment, strategic time-outs, weather interruptions and third-umpire reviews, will be exempt. The playing conditions also strengthen opportunities for regional cricketers. Each Playing XI must include at least two UAE players, two Afghanistan players and one player from an ICC Associate Member nation. This minimum combination must be maintained during substitutions and Super Sub changes, with specific provisions for concussion replacements. The fifth edition of the tournament will run from November 21 to December 20, 2026, featuring six franchises and several prominent international players.

sports.title: Anthony Davis Reportedly Wants To Return To Lakers, But A Reunion Is Unlikely
sports.description: Mandatory Credit: Brad Mills-Imagn Images Washington Wizards star Anthony Davis spent five and a half seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers , and it appears he might want a reunion. Brian Windhorst recently appeared on ESPN LA’s The Sedano & Kap Morning Show , where co-host Scott Kaplan told him he’d overheard reporters in the media room at a Lakers game talking about Davis wanting to come back to Los Angeles. “They don’t realize I’m listening and I’m hearing what they’re saying,” Kaplan said. “[One of them said], ‘I hear that Anthony Davis wants to return to the Lakers.’… I think they’re credentialized. I think they know what they’re talking about. They assume I have no idea. But Windy, could Anthony Davis… We always talk about another big man for the Lakers. “A, have you heard it?” Kaplan continued. “And B, is there a world where that could happen?” Windhorst rightly pointed out that Kaplan was talking about gossip in the press room. As for whether Davis and the Lakers could reunite, the 48-year-old doesn’t see it happening. “Very unlikely,” Windhorst said. “Anthony Davis is one of the bigger question marks in the league this year. There’s like three guys we’re watching, sort of star-level players about will they get traded. One is Anthony Davis, one is Kyrie Irving, Domantas Sabonis is on there. All of them are in the same boat. “All of them have options in their contract for next season,” Windhorst continued. “… The Wizards basically said, ‘We want to see Anthony Davis play 20 to 30 games, see how he fits with our group, and then we’re going to revisit about whether we want to give him a contract extension.’ Obviously, if they give him a contract extension, he agrees to it, he’s not being traded. “If he doesn’t get a contract extension, then I think you’re going to see his name out there on the trade market,” Windhorst added. “But here’s the thing. The Lakers just don’t have much high value things, forget about Anthony, just for any for any star player. They just don’t have much to trade. They’ve traded all of their picks for the most part.” Even if we ignore the lack of assets aspect for a bit, Davis is making $58.4 million in 2026-27. The Lakers won’t be trading Luka Doncic , Austin Reaves , or Walker Kessler to the Wizards for him, which makes matching salaries a very difficult task. They only have three other players making over $10 million in 2026-27: Quentin Grimes , Sandro Mamukelashvili , and Jarred Vanderbilt . Their combined salary is $39.3 million. The Lakers would have to give up most of their quality role players to get to $58 million. Even if they decide to do that, the Wizards would then have to see enough value in those players to send Davis to Los Angeles. The Lakers also gave up two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps to get Kessler from the Utah Jazz in the summer, so a 2032 first-round pick swap is the only valuable draft asset they can include in a package. While the Detroit Red Wings continue searching for an acceptable return for their former captain, a source has floated a potential trade framework involving veteran center Pavel Zacha , defenseman Mason Lohrei , or a first-round draft pick. There is a catch, of course. Actually, there are several. According to reporting from James Murphy of The Sick Podcast , Boston has been pushing harder to enter the Larkin sweepstakes. However, the Bruins reportedly have no interest in surrendering prized young center James Hagens, a player Detroit is believed to covet. That raises an obvious question: Could Boston satisfy the Red Wings without sacrificing one of its most promising young players? sports.title: Maresca ‘concerned’ after Man City suffer third league loss in a row
sports.description: Manchester City Coach Enzo Maresca gives an interview prior to the start of the UEFA Champions League soccer match between RB Leipzig and Manchester City at Red Bull Arena. (is associated with: «Maresca ‘concerned’ after Man City suffer third league loss in a row») Jan Woitas/dpa Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca is concerned about his side’s form after they suffered a third Premier League defeat in a row by going down 3-1 at Nottingham Forest. City won their opening seven games of the season but followed up defeats to Aston Villa and Brighton with a poor reverse at the City Ground. They were 2-0 down inside 18 minutes as Jair Cunha and Liam Delap scored before Rayan Cherki’s fine strike after the break gave them hope. But Delap’s second on the counter-attack killed the game and left Maresca’s side six points off leaders Arsenal. “I’m always concerned, even when we win games,” the Italian said. “We need to have balance. We won seven in a row. Now we have lost three in a row, so we need balance on that." “During the international break, try to understand what we can do better, and try to start again after the international break." “In the same way we have done the first one, we’re going to use this international break to try to clarify what we can do better," he addded. “We know we do some things better, and also we know we need to improve things. So we are going to use that and try to understand how we can avoid these kind of games,” he continued. Maresca revealed Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol were replaced at half-time due to injury. “Both injury, both asked for a change,” he said. “Marc Guehi an injury. Josko Gvardiol had some issue already during the week, so it was just because they had problems.” The victory could be a coming of age for Delap and Forest, who have struggled to adapt to life under new boss Oliver Glasner, with just one win from their opening nine games. Delap had scored once in eight games following his club-record move from Chelsea, but his brilliant double proved he can be the man to fire Forest to better things this season. “It’s now for Liam to keep working, getting into his best shape,” Glasner said. “Let’s say getting back to the Liam Delap he has been at Ipswich, and then even of course improving his game and he has still a lot to improve. “Definitely not his finishing with left and right, but he has to improve his heading, he has to improve his movements in the box. “He has to improve his understanding what we’re doing out of possession. But, also very honestly, he did very well.” Glasner reacted to Delap’s second goal with a touchline sprint to join in the celebrations. The Austrian said: “Of course, I can’t demand from the players they have to outrun the opposition, and I run less than the opposite manager. So I think I had to follow. “I just was told they were running six or seven kilometres more than City today, and that means I had to run more than Enzo Maresca as well, and I did my job. It was funny for me.”

sports.title: Indiana Pacers Can Now Afford To Sign A Free Agent. Should They?
sports.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 02: Quenton Jackson #29 of the Indiana Pacers makes a move on Corey Kispert #24 of the Atlanta Hawks at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on November 02, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty Images INDIANAPOLIS – The Indiana Pacers can now afford to sign a veteran 15th player to their roster. But do they need to do it right now? That’s the question the team’s front office is considering. Entering the season, the Pacers team spending level was over the luxury tax line and, of all importance for their roster size, near the first apron. That first apron acts as a hard cap for Indiana because they used a specific salary cap exception to sign wing Kelly Oubre in the offseason. When the season began, the Pacers had $206.8 million committed in terms of guaranteed contracts and possible salary bonuses. The first apron is just over $209 million. That left the team with a bit over $2.2 million in space between their roster spending and their hard cap. The veteran’s minimum for the entire 2026-27 NBA season is just shy of $2.45 million. That meant the Pacers couldn’t even afford to sign a player to a minimum-salary agreement when the season began – only a player with zero (and drafted in the second round) or one year of service could have been added to their team at the time. As a result, the Pacers carried 14 players on their roster to begin the season. But once the regular season starts, every passing day makes minimum contracts cheaper. They pro-rate based on how much of the season remains. And so earlier this week, a veteran’s minimum contract became small enough in remaining value that the Pacers could afford to sign any available free agent to a one-year contract. But the question remains: Should they? Entering the season, the answer to an early-as-possible addition seemed like it should be no. Just because the Pacers could sign someone doesn’t mean they should. Because minimum contracts pro-rate, as noted above, every passing day gives the Pacers more flexibility. For example, if the team opted to sign a player on the first possible day they could have, and that player stayed with the team for the rest of the season, the Pacers (essentially) couldn’t take back more salary than they sent out in trades or signed a player to a 10-day contract if they opened a roster spot – among many other transactions that would have become harder or impossible by using (basically) all of their remaining apron space at the first possible instant. The Pacers can – if they’re able to keep avoiding a signing – keep more team-building avenues open by waiting. Between slightly imbalanced trades, short-term signings, and other considerations related to their Mid-Level Exception, there are plenty of reasons to wait. sports.title: Chiefs Get Triple Injury Blow on Defense Before Week 9 Clash With Jets
sports.description: Cornerback Mansoor Delane logged 27 tackles and an interception across five starts, while rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods added 13 tackles and a half-sack in seven games to anchor Kansas City’s defense. Behind their contributions, the Chiefs built a top-tier run defense, allowing just 96.3 rushing yards per game this season. However, following a frustrating loss to the Denver Broncos, Kansas City now faces a sudden depth crisis. The latest defensive injuries force Kansas City to shuffle its personnel ahead of the matchup against the New York Jets. Mansoor Delane and two others miss Jets clash due to injuries Heading into Week 9, the Kansas City defense faces a sudden roster crunch as official injury reports confirm three key starters will sit out the upcoming matchup against New York. Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Mansoor Delane (5) celebrates with defensive end George Karlaftis (56) after a play against the Seattle Seahawks during the first half of the game at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Chiefs confirmed the status in their Week 9 update: “Nikko Remigio is questionable to play Sunday against the New York Jets. Peter Woods, Mansoor Delane, and Omarr Norman-Lott are out,” the team announced . Woods is dealing with a neck injury, Delane has a shoulder issue and Norman-Lott is listed with a knee injury. Andy Reid said Woods and Delane are progressing, but neither will play Sunday. “Both those two… are making progress, and that’s a positive thing, but they’re going to be out this game. It’s just a matter of getting back and making sure they’re strong; both of them, it’s a strength thing right now,” Reid said. Delane’s absence removes a first-round corner from the secondary. Kansas City selected the LSU product sixth overall in 2026. He has one interception and five pass breakups. Woods was also a first-round pick. His 13 tackles, half-sack, and pass breakup have supported the interior rotation. Norman-Lott’s absence further reduces the rotation and places more work on Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga. Remigio has 274 yards on 10 kick returns and 70 yards on 12 punt returns, giving Kansas City field-position value. The Chiefs enter after a 28-24 loss in Denver, their second defeat of the season after a 5-0 start. They allowed 11 penalties for 105 yards, and personal fouls helped Denver score 18 points. Sunday’s game at Arrowhead will test Steve Spagnuolo’s rotation. The Chiefs need replacements to protect the run defense, limit big plays, and avoid short fields. Their communication will matter against a Jets offense that has scored 58 points since Week 7. sports.title: 'A shared vision': LASA boys pace each other to Class 5A UIL state cross-country title
sports.description: The LASA boys team, flanked by Stacia Crescenzi, LASA's principal and assistant coach Sarah Davis on the left and head cross country coach Mary Beth Metcalf and assistant coach Kitty Kistler on the right, stand on the podium after winning the Class 5A state championship at the UIL state cross-country championships at Old Settler's Park in Round Rock, Texas. (Brom Hoban/Special to American-Statesman) ROUND ROCK - Over two cool, breezy days at Old Settler's Park, more than 1,500 of the state's best high school distance runners competed in the UIL state cross-country championships. And while there were a number of standout performances from Central Texas runners, it was Austin's LASA Raptors who rose to the pinnacle, capturing first place in Saturday's Class 5A race. The Raptors were led by senior Liam Brandyberry, who finished seventh overall in 15 minutes, 28 seconds on the rolling 5K course. "It took preparation, drive, commitment, character and courage to do what they had to do today, which is not easy," LASA head cross-country coach Mary Beth Metcalf said of the boys team, which also consisted of seniors Joaquin Gonzalez, John Wilson, Cruz Alcorta and Hugo Radjef, and juniors Ben Vazquez and Sam Smith. "Not so much a tactical approach, it was more about being committed to one another," Metcalf added. "During the race, when it feels overwhelming, when they feel like maybe they can't hang on any longer, when their brains are telling them to let up, I ask them to think about one another and the love that they have for their teammates, and to let that teammate commitment be what drives them forward. Our team has a shared commitment and obligation to will it into reality. It's a shared vision." Only the top five runners from each team have their finishing places added together to calculate the team score; the team with the lowest total score wins. LASA scored 94 points, ahead of runner-up Weslaco East's 98 and third-place Dallas Wilson's 113. Weslaco East's Alexander Nava won the overall race in 15 minutes, 13 seconds, while Georgetown's Matthew Morales averaged 4:56 per mile to grab second in 15:18. Liberty Hill's Zander Radziwon was 11th (15:40) and Lockhart's Ethan Herrera (15:52) was 19th. "These boys, since they've been freshmen, they've always felt like a team and worked together like a team," LASA principal Stacia Crescenzi said. "What makes this so emotional today is not that they won, but that they did it together." sports.description: Motorsport photo Max Verstappen called it a day after Q1 during Formula 1 qualifying in Sao Paulo, as he already knew he would be starting from the back of the grid for the Brazilian Grand Prix due to an engine-related grid penalty. In the FIA's 'indicative grid', Verstappen is listed in 21st place, behind Lewis Hamilton and just ahead of Sergio Perez . The four-time world champion once again demonstrated in Q1 just how competitive he can be in wet conditions. His first flying lap was 1.4 seconds faster than the time at the top of the leaderboard at that point, and four tenths quicker than Hamilton, who crossed the start-finish line shortly afterwards. The Red Bull driver eventually finished the opening segment of qualifying in third place – behind Lando Norris and George Russell – before climbing out of the car. Read Also: Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen hit with F1 grid penalties for Brazilian GP Asked whether he had at least enjoyed himself to some extent in the Brazilian rain, Verstappen replied in the media pen: "Not really, because I'm not fighting for anything. My mind is already set on tomorrow, so it was just about doing a lap, not risking anything. Every lap that I did, we were up there, but for me that's not a surprise." Like his fellow drivers, Verstappen had to wait almost an hour and a half because of the red-flag delay before he could even get out on track. Asked how he had spent that time during the heavy rainfall, Verstappen laughed in front of Viaplay's camera: "Watching football. Premier League." Asked which match he had been watching exactly, Verstappen continued: "A lot of different games, but Nottingham Forest-Manchester City was the last one before I got into the car. It was 3-1, I actually saw a great goal just before I got back in!" When it was pointed out that fans might find it hard to believe Verstappen had been watching football shortly before having to tackle qualifying in extremely difficult conditions, the Dutchman responded calmly: "But I'm starting last anyway, so it doesn’t matter. I’ve lost 12 hours of my life today that I’ll never get back." Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Why Verstappen believes a comeback drive will be harder in 2026 While there was nothing at stake for Verstappen on Saturday, Sunday will naturally be a different matter. Verstappen has already produced three memorable comeback races at Interlagos, including in the past two seasons. In 2024, Verstappen won from 17th on the grid, effectively nipping Norris's remaining title ambitions in the bud, while last year the Dutchman drove from the pitlane to the podium. Starting from the back row therefore does not necessarily mean he has no chance, but Verstappen believes fighting his way through the field with the 2026 cars will be considerably more difficult. sports.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams Hit With NFL Fines
sports.description: The Detroit Lions picked up a hard-fought 19-15 victory over the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8, but two of their biggest offensive stars are now paying a price for their actions during the game. On Saturday, the NFL announced that wide receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams were each fined $11,941 for taunting during Detroit’s November 1 victory at Ford Field. That’s a combined $23,882 in fines for the Lions’ dynamic receiving duo. Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams (1) reacts to a penalty after a first down celebration against Minnesota Vikings during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit Lions Receivers Fined for Taunting According to the NFL’s official accountability report , both violations occurred during the first quarter. Amon-Ra St. Brown: $11,941 for taunting with 11:25 remaining in the first quarter. Jameson Williams: $11,941 for taunting with 4:55 remaining in the first quarter. Williams’ penalty came following a 46-yard reception from Jared Goff that moved Detroit deep into Minnesota territory. However, the receiver was flagged after spinning the football near a Vikings defender, costing the Lions 15 yards. St. Brown was penalized earlier in the quarter after standing over a Minnesota defender following a running play. Both incidents resulted in unsportsmanlike conduct penalties during the game. Jameson Williams Has Been Here Before Interestingly, this isn’t the first time Williams has found himself dealing with the NFL’s disciplinary process this season. Earlier in the year, Williams was assessed fines totaling $26,867 for taunting and an illegal celebration during Detroit’s Week 2 loss to Buffalo. However, the receiver successfully appealed both fines , resulting in those penalties being rescinded. Whether Williams or St. Brown will appeal their latest fines remains to be seen. Despite the penalties, Detroit ultimately got the result it wanted against Minnesota. As we previously reported following the victory , Williams caught the go-ahead touchdown pass from Goff in the fourth quarter, helping the Lions hand the Vikings their first loss of the season. The victory also improved Detroit’s record to 5-2, with the Lions leaning heavily on a rushing attack that piled up 230 yards . The NFL has made it clear that taunting violations can carry consequences beyond the field. For St. Brown and Williams, that lesson now comes with a combined $23,882 price tag, assuming the fines are upheld.

sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold watches from the bench as Fede Valverde scores a stunner from right-back for Real Madrid
sports.description: Valencia CF v Real Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Trent Alexander-Arnold joined Real Madrid to become their first-choice right-back, but under Jose Mourinho he is now watching a midfielder do that job instead. Captain Fede Valverde started there again at Mestalla and smashed in the opener against Valencia, while Alexander-Arnold and summer signing Denzel Dumfries were left out of the starting XI once again. Valverde strikes from right-back at Mestalla Valverde lined up at right-back for Real Madrid's trip to Valencia on Saturday, with neither Alexander-Arnold nor Dumfries in Mourinho's starting XI. The Uruguayan made the call look inspired in the 28th minute, when Kylian Mbappe's free-kick was blocked by the wall and the ball rolled back to the Real Madrid captain. Valverde controlled the ball around 20 metres out and drilled a powerful low strike into the net. Arda Guler doubled the lead eight minutes later, and the visitors went in at the break 2-0 up. Captain dominates in an unfamiliar role Valverde's display was about far more than his goal. According to Sofascore, he had 32 touches in the first half, completed 26 of his 29 passes and was not dribbled past once, while Real Madrid enjoyed 75 per cent of possession. It was the latest sign that Mourinho's experiment has become a settled plan. Valverde was first moved to right-back during the 1-0 win over Villarreal last month and has since started there against Sevilla, RB Leipzig and Barcelona, as well as at Mestalla. Alexander-Arnold's minutes dry up The shift has hit Alexander-Arnold hardest. The England international has played just 435 minutes in all competitions this season, with only four starts in La Liga, and he was an unused substitute in Real Madrid's last three Champions League games. His only start since the Villarreal game came in the 3-0 win at Racing Santander , when Valverde missed out with muscular discomfort. It is a sharp fall for a player who made 30 appearances last season despite a string of injuries, while Dumfries has also lost his place only months after arriving. What next for the sidelined full-backs? Real Madrid had won seven games in a row in all competitions before kick-off, so Mourinho has little reason to change a winning side. Speaking at his press conference before the Racing game, he insisted: "In the end, everyone will play." Alexander-Arnold can count on England. Thomas Tuchel left him out of his World Cup squad but has since recalled him, and he played 90 minutes in both wins over the Czech Republic during the last international break. England face Croatia on Thursday.

sports.title: Norris grabs pole in rainswept qualifying for Sao Paulo Grand Prix
sports.description: McLaren's British driver Lando Norris celebrates after securing pole position for the Sao Paulo Formula One Grand Prix (Nelson ALMEIDA) McLaren's outgoing world champion Lando Norris grabbed pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix with a brave and well-judged drive in Saturday's rainswept qualifying at Interlagos. The 26-year-old Briton clocked a best lap in one minute and 27.470 seconds to outpace George Russell of Mercedes by 0.204 seconds as heavy rain curtailed Q3 at the end of a session that lasted almost two and a half hours. New world champion Kimi Antonelli was third for Mercedes, but he will start Sunday's race from the front row as Russell faces a five-place grid penalty for taking new power-unit components. It is the 20th pole position of Norris's career and his third in succession in Brazil. "It's been a long day," said Norris. "It's been a great qualifying, to be on pole again here, two years in a row! Different conditions to last year, but I am very happy. "It was about getting two laps in and not making a mistake and that is exactly what we did so it has been a very good day." Russell was disappointed not to take pole after being told by Mercedes to ease off on his final push lap. "Congrats to Lando, but it was definitely my pole lap. We should have finished the lap." Antonelli said: "It was very tricky out there and, to be fair, I didn't know what to expect as I have never driven here before in the wet. I made a mistake and I nearly went off!" Charles Leclerc was fourth for Ferrari but also faces a penalty of 10 places for taking a new engine. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson was fifth ahead of Audi's Nico Hulkenberg, Isack Hadjar of Red Bull and Oliver Bearman's Haas. science.title: NASA Seeks Next Generation of Explorers to Join Astronaut Corps
science.description: NASA announced its 2025 Astronaut Candidate Class on Sept. 22, 2025, at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Credit: NASA/Helen Arase Vargas NASA is looking for the explorers who will help write the next chapter of human spaceflight. Applications are now open for the agency’s next class of astronauts, who will join NASA as America returns to the Moon, builds the Moon Base, and lays the groundwork for the first crewed missions to Mars. The next generation of astronauts will train to operate on the lunar surface, live and work beyond Earth, and take on missions that will push the boundaries of human exploration farther than ever before. U.S. citizens interested in joining the astronaut corps have until 11:59 p.m. EST Thursday, Dec. 3, to submit their completed application materials at: https://go.nasa.gov/3WyvlQi “This is an extraordinary time to join NASA’s astronaut corps,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “The people we select could walk on the Moon, live and work at the Moon Base, and help pioneer the systems and operations that will ultimately carry crews to Mars. Those missions will demand technical excellence, sound judgment, teamwork, and courage. NASA’s astronaut corps has always called on remarkable Americans willing to take on extraordinary challenges in service to the nation. If you are ready to join that tradition, come help write the next chapter of humanity’s greatest adventure.” NASA expects to make its final selection in late 2027 to begin training as the next class of astronaut candidates. “The window is open. The mission is waiting. And the only thing missing from the greatest adventure humanity has ever embarked upon is you,” said NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson. The agency last opened applications in 2024. From more than 8,000 applications, 10 astronaut candidates were selected in 2025 and are currently completing nearly two years of training. “For those who apply, becoming a NASA astronaut is more than a career opportunity,” said Scott Tingle, chief astronaut and chair of the Astronaut Selection Board at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. “It is a chance to join a legacy of explorers who have pushed the boundaries of discovery and play a role in the missions that will shape humanity’s future in space. The next generation of astronaut candidates could help write history while inspiring future scientists, engineers, and explorers.” Since the 1960s, NASA has selected 370 people to train as astronaut candidates for its increasingly challenging missions. The agency has 32 astronauts active in the astronaut corps, and selected applicants will join their ranks to study spacewalking, lunar geology, operations of high-performance aircraft, and more. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." science.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
science.description: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. Star Wars Zero Company and Galactic Racer 's restrained scope and confidence have been infectious, and, as it turns out, they're already recognized by all the parties involved as double-A success stories . Now this is podracing! (Image credit: Secret Mode) A Burnout-inspired Star Wars racer (created by a bunch of ex-Burnout devs) is a fantastic pitch if you know your video games, but looking at EA's recent and current direction, it's easy to see why it didn't happen under their reign. The original Burnout studio, Criterion, would have been an excellent candidate, but instead they were sent to work in the Battlefield mines. Still, someone was interested in the idea, and the end result is glorious. Fast and furious, Star Wars: Galactic Racer ignores recent racing game trends and bets big on arcade-y vibes, uncomplicated controls, and a high skill ceiling that challenges you with extremely high speeds, tight turns, and unexpected interruptions as other drivers try to ruin your day. The not-so-secret sauce, however, was its runs-based structure, which injects the flexibility and replay value of roguelite games into the more traditional arcade racing structure that older gamers are familiar with. (Image credit: EA) Fully confident in its central gameplay idea and devoid of modern live-service baggage, Fuse Games' debut title makes the most of the Star Wars setting within the restrictions of simply making a fun and engaging Star Wars racer. It's almost the same approach we felt in Zero Company, a turn-based tactical strategy-RPG that comes from the minds of another team of ex-triple-A developers. "Star Wars but XCOM" should've happened earlier, but we're glad it did this year, and, unsurprisingly, it's a banger. The correct read of their success should be obvious (and so far, it appears the powers that be are seeing it): Let seasoned and fresh developers cook games they're excited about. Big, medium, or small, players will react positively to experiences that really feel genuine and aren't brought down by tacked-on systems or monetization.
